title: Maritime security in focus at India-Belgium naval talks
author: PTI
content_html:
Commander of the Belgian Navy, Rear Admiral Tanguy Botman, held talks with Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan on a range of issues, including maritime security, operational engagements, and collaboration in naval technology, officials said on Saturday (November 15, 2026).

The bilateral talk was aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation and further deepening navy-to-navy engagements between the two countries.

On arrival, he paid homage to fallen soldiers by laying a wreath at the National War Memorial. Thereafter, he was accorded a ceremonial guard of honour at the South Block lawns.

He also interacted with other senior officials to explore avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation. India and Belgium share longstanding maritime linkages.

The visit marks an important milestone in bilateral navy-to-navy relations and is expected to provide impetus to maritime cooperation through strengthening existing engagements and exploration of new avenues for collaboration, the official said.

title: Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises
author: Vinaya Deshpande Pandit
content_html:
The cotton plants are green, but the bolls are missing. Across the Chauhan family’s four-acre field in Majalgaon in Maharashtra’s Beed district, the plants stand stunted, their promise of a harvest withered by the absence of rain. What should have been a season of cotton picking has become a search for the few bolls the drought has spared.

Under the relentless October sun, Vanita Chauhan bends over the plants, picking the little cotton she can find. A tattered towel covers her head, shielding her from the scorching heat. Her full-sleeved shirt is buttoned up to her neck, while the red pallu of her sari is tied around her arm and neck, fashioned into an improvised pouch. She drops each cotton boll into it before moving hurriedly to the next plant.

title: In Jharkhand, even jails are not safe: Babulal Marandi
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
The Leader of the Opposition in the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on Saturday (November 14, 2026), cornered the State Government over a series of criminal incidents.

He cited the incidents of including the sexual assault of a youth in Hotwar Jail, the alleged rape of a minor girl by a Congress MLA from Simdega, and the alleged rape of a woman who had gone to the Gamharia police station seeking justice.

Fifteen police officers were suspended in connection with the alleged rape of a 20-year-old woman on the premises of the Gamharia police station in Jharkhand, Saraikela-Kharsawan district, on November 1, 2026.

Launching a sharp attack on Sorens’ government, Mr. Marandi said law and order in Jharkhand has collapsed and it raises serious questions on the functioning of the government.

Addressing a press conference at the state Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) office in Ranchi, Mr. Marandi said that such incidents are continuously coming to light, and they are deeply disturbing.

“Today, in Jharkhand, neither jails nor police stations nor the residences of legislators are safe. What has happened to Jharkhand? How have conditions in the state deteriorated to such an extent that ordinary citizens no longer feel safe anywhere?” Mr. Marandi said.

‘Prisoners are not safe even in jail’

Expressing concern over the incident at Hotwar Jail, Mr. Marandi asserted that while a jail is considered the most secure place, even there, prisoners are not safe.

A man has recently filed a police complaint against 19 people, including Birsa Munda Central Jail officials, alleging severe abuse of his 20-year-old son inside the jail.

The father had accused jail inmates and staff of sexual assault of his son and forced him to consume narcotics while he stayed there as an undertrial prisoner.

“A 20-year-old youth was allegedly subjected to gang sexual assault. This incident is truly chilling. When the victim filed a written complaint, it was torn, and he was not even provided with proper medical treatment,” Mr. Marandi said.

He added that he had previously written to the government regarding incidents involving women at Hotwar Jail as well. Mr. Marandi further mentioned that even the court took cognisance of the matter, but instead of taking action and ensuring accountability, the government attempted to cover it up.

Senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader demanded the immediate removal of all responsible jail officials and the transfer of the accused inmates to another prison.

Reacting to the allegations against a Congress MLA, Bhushan Bara from Simdega, Mr. Marandi said that since the case involves an MLA from the Congress party, which is part of the ruling coalition, the government is under pressure.

Mr. Marandi mentioned that he had met with the victim, who shared her ordeal with him. He alleged that the MLA’s wife and sister also physically assaulted the girl. Mr. Marandi demanded an impartial investigation and strict action against those found guilty.

Hours after an FIR was registered against Mr. Bara on the charge of raping his minor domestic help, police said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that they booked two persons for allegedly abducting and coercing the girl into making a “false” statement against the legislator.

427 deaths in police custody

Raising the issue of deaths occurring in police and judicial custody, Mr. Marandi said that, according to a report submitted by the state government to the Jharkhand High Court, 427 individuals died in police or judicial custody by 2026.

“Notably, 262 of these cases were not subjected to a judicial inquiry; instead, they were investigated by an executive magistrate. On May 14, 2026, the High Court had expressed deep displeasure and had directed that 262 cases be investigated afresh within six months,” Mr. Marandi said.

He added that despite the expiry of the deadline, no clear information regarding the progress of these investigations has emerged.

title: Mumbai police announce traffic diversion ahead of Britain’s Prince William visit
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Mumbai Police on Saturday (November 14, 2026) have announced traffic diversions, road closures and parking restrictions across parts of south Mumbai from November 16 to 19 in view of a VVIP visit to the city. The restrictions come ahead of Britain’s Prince William’s visit to Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony.

The ceremony is hosted in Mumbai from November 16 to 18 for the sixth annual Earthshot Prize.

The notification issued by Hemrajsingh Rajput, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South), Traffic, Mumbai, includes changes to traffic movement around Hutatma Rajguru Chowk, Shaheed Bhagatsingh Marg, Ballard Pier and several roads in the NCPA area.

The pay and park are suspended on Vinay K. Shah Marg road and Dorabji Tata Road for 24 hours, and on November 16, the parking is suspended from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Moraji Road, J. N. Media Marg, and Walchand Hirachand Marg.

The U-turn from Free Press Road’s northbound carriageway at Hutatma Rajguru Chowk towards the southbound carriageway will be permitted during this period and the right turn from Madam Cama Road towards Free press road will remain open.

The restrictions were also made on the movement of vehicles towards the Ballard Pier alighting point on November 16. From 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., the route from Shahid Bhagat Singh Marg to Avtarsingh Bedi Chowk and then right towards Walchand Hirachand Marg will remain open only to vehicles carrying VVIPs.

title: 4.5 magnitude earthquake tremors felt in Maharashtra’s Jalgaon
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Maharashtra’s Jalgaon district felt earthquake tremors of 4.6 magnitude on Saturday (November 14, 2026), raising concerns among the citizens, the district officials said on Tuesday. Palghar is located 100 km from Mumbai.

The tremors were felt at around 9.16 a.m. in the Satpuda region, including Yawal, Raver, Chopda and Bhusawal taluka, with its epicentre located in Madhya Pradesh’s Khargone district. District Collector Rohan Ghuge said, “No loss of life or property damage in Jalgaon has been reported. Residents should not panic or fall prey to any rumours.”

Jalgaon also houses three major dams, including Hatnur, Waghur and Girna. One of the concerns was potential seismic risks in these regions due to the tremors. However, nothing happened, cleared the Jalgaon District officials,

Earlier in August, Maharashtra’s Palghar felt two back-to-back tremors of magnitude 3.4 in a span of an hour. Palghar is located 400 km from Mumbai.

title: Man held for conducting ‘reconnaissance’ of sensitive locations in Mumbai
author: PTI
content_html:
A 20-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of sensitive locations in Mumbai, including the Chabad House, a Jewish community centre, on the instructions of international criminal syndicates and anti-national elements, an official said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Yash Singh, a resident of Airoli in Navi Mumbai, was initially detained by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) based on inputs regarding his social media contacts with anti-national handlers.

He was subsequently taken into custody by the Keralam police in connection with a case registered in the Thrissur district in the southern state, the official said.

Singh told the police that he was tasked by social media handlers linked to mafia gangs and subversive elements to carry out a recce of sensitive areas of South Mumbai, particularly around Colaba.

“His assignments included photographing and pinpointing the exact locations of the Chabad House, businesses owned by Jewish individuals, and areas frequented by foreign nationals. He received money in exchange for these activities,” the official said.

Chabad House was among the locations targeted by Pakistani terrorists during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks in 2008.

Further investigation established that Singh was allegedly in direct contact with anti-national elements through the messaging platform Telegram, linking him to an accused already arrested in a case registered at the Thrissur East police station in Keralam under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).

Alerted by the ATS, a team from the Thrissur police arrived in Navi Mumbai and formally placed him under arrest after confirming his direct involvement in the conspiracy, the official said.

According to officials, crime syndicates operating from abroad, such as the Pakistan-based ‘Shahzad Bhatti Network’, have been using platforms like Telegram, Instagram, and WhatsApp to look for unemployed and financially vulnerable youths for reconnaissance and subversive activities.

ATS officials have urged parents and young citizens to remain vigilant, avoid engaging with unknown contacts online, and refrain from sharing photographs or information about sensitive locations for monetary gain.
